claim_verdicts.evidence: git show stage-1:samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Design/OrderNotifications.cs: line 11 `private readonly EmailNotifier notifier = new();` in OrderPlacedTightlyCoupled; line 20 `public sealed class OrderNotifications(INotifier notifier)`; lines 20-23 contain no `new`.

refs csharp-12.md: "You can now create primary constructors in any `class` and `struct`. ... Primary constructor parameters are in scope for the entire body of the class." Tutorial: "You can add parameters to a `struct` or `class` declaration to create a *primary constructor*." Projects target net10.0 (C# 14 per versions.yaml), so the feature applies.

OrdersController.cs:12 `public sealed class OrdersController(OrderService orderService, IOrderRepository repository) : ControllerBase`; OrderService.cs:6 `public sealed class OrderService(...)`; IOrderRepository.cs: `public interface IOrderRepository`.

OrderService.cs:6 `public sealed class OrderService(IOrderRepository repository, INotifier notifier)`. The only `new` in the file: `new ArgumentException`, `new Order { ... }`, `new KeyNotFoundException` — none create a repository or notifier. OrdersController's `new` calls are OrderItem/anonymous route values only.

`git grep -n OrderNotifications stage-1` outside the declaring file returns only a comment in DonHang.Domain/INotifier.cs:4. No `new OrderNotifications`/`OrderNotifications(` call anywhere in the repo, samples tests included.

EfOrderRepository.cs:7 `public sealed class EfOrderRepository(DonHangDbContext db) : IOrderRepository`; DonHangDbContext.cs:7 `public sealed class DonHangDbContext(DbContextOptions<DonHangDbContext> options) : DbContext(options)` — concrete (and sealed).

ASP.NET Core DI: "the dependency injection (DI) software design pattern, which is a technique for achieving Inversion of Control (IoC) between classes and their dependencies." Architectural principles: "The practice of *dependency injection* is made possible by following the dependency inversion principle." Injection of a concrete type is shown by OrdersController.cs:12 (OrderService).

Follows directly from the code shape: a field initialiser `= new EmailNotifier()` inside the class fixes the concrete type regardless of the declared field type; changing it requires editing that initialiser. Same point made and reviewed in design.l1.solid-dip.

dotnet architecture/maui DI: "a class constructor is invoked ... any values that the object needs are passed as arguments to the constructor. This is an example of dependency injection known as *constructor injection*." "There are also other types of dependency injection, such as *property setter injection* and *method call injection*, but they are less commonly seen." ASP.NET Core: "## Action injection with `FromServices`" — "enables injecting a service directly into an action method without using constructor injection".

issues.text: Round-1 major (constructor-only DI) is resolved in section 3 and summary line 1, but section 4 and summary line 2 still give 'through the constructor' as THE answer to how DI delivers the object, unqualified. Covered by section 3's 'in this course' framing, so only minor; the round-1 issue text named this sentence too.
issues.quote: DI asks how the object reaches the class, and answers: through the constructor, from outside.
issues.fix: Section 4: "DI asks how the object reaches the class, and answers: from outside, here through the constructor." Summary line 2: "...DI says how the object gets there (from outside, here through the constructor)."

issues.text: The explanation for option b reads awkwardly: 'would be a problem only when C# forbade them' sounds like a time condition, and I had to re-read it to see it means 'if C# forbade them, but it does not'. It does not change my answer.
issues.quote: Interface-typed fields would be a problem only when C# forbade them, and it does not: `OrderNotifications` stores an `INotifier`.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: 'C# allows fields of an interface type: `OrderNotifications` stores an `INotifier`.'
